name: elder tree

attributes.attribute: symbolic tree of the genus Sambucus
unlucky to burn, the home of fertility spirits
called the eller tree, linked to the elf people
offered rags in northern Britain for good luck

sources: Briggs, Katharine M. The Folklore of the Cotswolds. London: B. T. Batsford Ltd., 1974.
Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972, 107-108.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The elder is a symbolic tree. In most Celtic lands people considered it unlucky to burn elder wood. Fertility spirits, they held, lived within the elder of the genus Sambucus. Anyone forced to use elder wood had to ask the tree's permission first. Branches might bleed even then. The name links the elder to the elf people. In northern Britain people called it the eller tree and offered it rags for good luck.
